Our opportunity is to reinvent systems of record for an agentic world, not just build new experiences on top of them, while giving every business an entirely new way to orchestrate work and build what is missing. I believe all this can reset business SaaS. That is the direction we are taking at Microsoft: Copilot as a new OS for work, with a governed infinite SaaS factory built in.

[Prince Gupta](https://in.linkedin.com/in/iprincengupta?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 24m


The "systems of record" line is the real shift. In customer engagement, the conversation happens on WhatsApp and Instagram, but the record lives in the CRM or ticketing tool. Agents that only sit on top inherit that gap. The ones that write back to the record, with state and an audit trail, close it. Curious how governance keeps up when the factory ships apps faster than IT can review them.


[Maria Cong](https://www.linkedin.com/in/maria-cong-429686399?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 23m


This is a paradigm shift. Treating Copilot as the OS for work turns static SaaS applications into composable, agent-driven workflows.


[Reply](https://www.linkedin.com/signup/cold-join?session_redirect=https%3A%2F%2Fwww%2Elinkedin%2Ecom%2Fposts%2Fsatyanadella_the-infinite-saas-factory-activity-7513980032831078400-dyiq&trk=public_post_comment_reply) 1 Reaction


[Fred Lusky](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fredriclusky?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 27m


What really caught my attention is the idea of people no longer having to work around their software. ⠀ We see this opportunity with SMS all the time. A customer needs an update, but the information is sitting in a CRM, an order system, or somewhere else entirely. Someone has to connect the dots before a simple text can go out. ⠀ Imagine AI agents handling that coordination automatically, pulling the right information, following the right rules, and starting a relevant conversation with the customer. ⠀ The exciting part isn't just building more software. It's finally getting the systems we already have to work together.


[Selfic-AI](https://www.linkedin.com/company/selficai?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 9m


Rebuilding systems of record for an agentic world, instead of just layering new experiences on top of them, is the bolder and harder path. Having governance built in from the start is what will make that credible for enterprises.


[Afaq Shahid](https://pk.linkedin.com/in/afaq-shahid-khan?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 46m


Reinventing systems of record is the bigger opportunity because agents need governed access to context and actions, not just another interface layered over legacy SaaS.


[Michał Piszczek](https://pl.linkedin.com/in/michalpiszczek?trk=public_post_comment_actor-name) 5m


Agents hit systems of record far more often than people do, so load and audit trails change before the UI does. Does the governed headless layer handle per-agent limits and rollback, or is that left to each app?
